Figure 3:Overview of PersistWorld.
Top: the world stateSSis updated once per capture group; the Evolver, marked E, carries it to the capture time of the next group, and the Writer, marked W, writes the new images into it;SSis reset to the initial state every eight capture groups.
To forecast, the Evolver predicts the state at a queried timetkt_{k}fromSSand the ego trajectory, and the Reader, marked R, decodes it in the queried ego frame.
Bottom: the internal operations of each component, Secs.3.2–3.4.
The grid loss supervises the current and future occupancy, and the ray loss supervises the ray-depth sections of the Writer.
Images and ground-truth occupancy, seen from above, are from a nuScenes validation scene.

Figure 7:Forecasts of our model and the ground truth (GT) in two scenes (a) and (b) of Occ3D-nuScenes, at the current frame and 1, 2, and 3 s ahead. Only voxels inside the camera mask of each target frame are drawn.

Figure 8:Forecasts of PersistWorld from one state along two trajectories at an intersection, at 1, 2, and 3 s ahead: (a) the recorded right turn and (b) straight ahead. All forecast voxels are drawn, since a trajectory that was not driven has no camera mask.

Figure 10:Two more scenes, drawn as inFig.9: (a) a right turn past cars parked along the curb; (b) pedestrians at an intersection.

Figure 11:Forecasts of PersistWorld and the ground truth in two failure cases, at the current frame and 1, 2, and 3 s ahead: (a) a car waiting ahead at an intersection drives off after the last input frame; (b) the ego vehicle drives into space that no input frame observed. Only voxels inside the camera mask of each target frame are drawn. Dashed outline in (a): where the car stood at the last input frame; hatching in (b): ground-truth space not observed in the input frames.
